input: Join a community litter-picking group this month

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether they want to simply sign up or also attend a first event changes how much needs to happen this month.
Their location (urban, suburban, rural) determines which groups exist and how easy they are to find.
Whether they are joining alone or with others (family, friends, colleagues) affects which group type suits them — e.g. family-friendly sessions vs. adult-only groups.
Their available days and times narrow down which groups' schedules are compatible.
Some people want a casual one-off participation; others want to become a regular committed member — this shapes which groups to target.
Whether they already have leads (known local groups, apps like LitterFree, council websites) or need to start from scratch changes the first action.
Defining what 'done' looks like — signed up online, attended one event, or made a recurring commitment — sets a clear finish line for this month.

gold.taskTitle: Join a local litter-picking group this month
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find and join a community litter-picking group within the current month.

questions.title: Does joining mean signed up, or attending a first event?
questions.description: Clarify whether the goal for this month is to register with a group, or to have physically attended at least one litter-pick.

questions.title: What area or neighbourhood are you based in?
questions.description: Identify the user's location to determine which local groups, council schemes, or community networks are realistically available.

questions.title: Will you be joining solo or with other people?
questions.description: Establish whether this is a solo activity or involves family, friends, or colleagues, to match the right type of group or session.

questions.title: Which days or times are you free to participate?
questions.description: Understand scheduling availability so that only groups running compatible sessions are considered.

questions.title: Do you want to commit regularly or try it once first?
questions.description: Find out whether the user is looking for a one-off taster or wants to become an ongoing member of a group.

questions.title: Have you already found any local groups or leads?
questions.description: Check whether the user has prior knowledge of groups, apps, or council contacts, so the plan starts at the right step.

questions.title: Should this include a specific area like a park or street?
questions.description: Determine whether the user has a particular location they care about cleaning up, which may point to niche local groups or self-organised efforts.
